## Conservation & rarity context

-   **Rarity note:** Common species in Florida, found in hardwood hammocks, cypress swamps, and other habitats with mature trees and water.

## Natural history notes

A large woodland owl characterized by its rounded head with no ear tufts, dark eyes, brown-and-white streaked body, and barred pattern across the chest and belly. In Florida, it is found in hardwood hammocks, cypress swamps, wooded wetlands, pine forests, forest edges, parks, and wooded neighborhoods, especially near mature trees and water. It feeds mainly on small mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, insects, and crayfish, usually hunting from a perch at night and capturing prey on the ground or in shallow water.
